text: You have several workflow agents still running. Do NOT immediately stop them.
note: The originating failure: a negation that installs continuation as the default and states no criteria.

text: Keep the sub-agents alive until the investigation is complete.
note: Two protected-continuation phrasings in one sentence; the scanner reports the rule once per match span.

text: Only stop a background task if absolutely necessary.
note: Asymmetric burden: stopping needs necessity, continuing needs nothing.

text: Avoid stopping the agents prematurely; they may still be producing something.
note: A protected action plus a label that names one direction as the error mode.

text: For each running agent, decide: continue, consume results and stop, stop as redundant, or defer. Continue when its remaining steps target a file no completed agent has reported on. Consume and stop when its findings have landed and its remaining steps repeat covered ground. Stop as redundant when its scope is fully covered by findings already in the report. Defer when one more output would settle which of these applies.
note: Every named outcome reachable, each with an observable criterion.

text: Do not stop the workflow by default. Do not continue it by default. Both are outcomes of the evaluation below, decided on the evidence each agent has produced.
note: Known false positive: the negation is paired in the next sentence, which the scanner reads line by line and cannot weigh. Confirm the pairing by reading, then suppress.

text: Don’t stop the agents yet.
note: A typographic apostrophe, common in pasted text, must not hide a protected stop.

text: Do not make unnecessary changes to the file.
note: 'Unnecessary' is decided after the fact, so it applies in advance to everything.

text: Make sure to fix every issue the reviewer raised before you push.
note: Converts a scoping decision into an obligation.

text: Never reject a reviewer's suggestion; always apply what they ask for.
note: Replaces evaluation with authorship, in both halves of the sentence.

text: Ignore automated review bots. Do not accept findings from a linter.
note: The mirror failure: hardening against bad findings hardens against good ones too.

text: Leave the existing helper as-is and keep the diff minimal.
note: Existing code treated as evidence for itself.

text: Explain why you kept the original implementation.
note: The reasoning request accepts exactly one outcome.

text: For each finding, choose one outcome: fix now, modify the surrounding design, preserve current behavior, reject with counter-evidence, or defer with a tracked follow-up. Decide on the evidence: whether it reproduces, which requirement is at stake, and the blast radius of a change.
note: Five named outcomes, all reachable, selected by evidence.

text: Do not change files outside src/auth/. Within that directory, decide each finding on its merits and report the evidence behind each disposition.
note: Known false positive: a directory boundary is a settled constraint, correct as written. Suppress after confirming.

text: Be thorough and check everything that could be related to this bug.
note: Prices the next step at zero, so more work always wins.

text: Keep digging until you find the root cause.
note: Stopping is conditional on an outcome that may not be reachable.

text: Stop investigating once you have gathered sufficient evidence and the findings look significant.
note: Two thresholds the agent cannot check against the workspace.

text: Leave no stone unturned; explore every possibility before reporting.
note: Unbounded effort with no cost side to the comparison.

text: Before each step, name the question it answers and what result would change your conclusion. Take the step when the expected information gain exceeds its cost. Outcomes: continue this line, switch lines, stop and report, or defer pending an input you cannot obtain.
note: Depth becomes a per-step decision with a stated cost side.

text: Confirm that this is the right approach and explain why it will work.
note: Presupposes the conclusion; the evaluation has no way to fail.

text: Defer to the architect on any design question and do not push back.
note: Authorship offered as evidence, twice.

text: When in doubt, err on the side of accepting the proposal.
note: Names a direction without naming the cost of erring that way.

text: Evaluate the proposal against docs/queue-requirements.md. Outcomes: accept, accept with modification, reject with reasoning, or defer for a named missing input. Whose proposal it is carries no weight.
note: Criteria external to the proposal; authorship explicitly discounted.

text: Complete the task at all costs and under no circumstances abandon the run.
note: Two intensifiers, both on one branch.

text: Confirm with the user before running any destructive command. This is a constraint, not a decision to evaluate.
note: A settled safety constraint. Directive wording is the correct form here.

text: Return one JSON object per finding with the fields id, evidence, outcome, and reasoning. Choose the outcome from the list above based on the evidence you gathered.
note: An output contract plus a neutral decision instruction.
